result: PASS component and actual-QEMU timing tests; live latency measurement pending
bug: Rescheduling next byte at callback dispatch time + byte period loses elapsed wire time whenever the main loop dispatches a timer late.

deterministic_delayed_dispatch.test_origin: Exact UART section extracted from virt.c, compiled with deterministic timer/character adapters and ASan/UBSan. Not a full-QEMU delayed-mainloop test.

qtest.semantics: qtest clock_step and clock_set walk each intermediate deadline via qemu_clock_advance_virtual_time. They do not simulate late dispatch, so the old implementation passes normal pacing tests too.

change: Retain next-byte deadline and admit elapsed bytes in a loop bounded by FIFO free capacity. Empty ingress or full FIFO clears carried deadline. Reading FIFO schedules future delivery only; no inline refill. Backpressure restarts at now + one byte period. TX behavior unchanged.
coverage: Delayed callback accounts for elapsed wire time
Full FIFO backpressure without accumulated delivery credit
All ingress bytes delivered in order
Idle to new burst starts with one complete byte period
Receive IRQ clears on empty FIFO
limitations: No live guest restart or mutation by these tests
This fixes modeled RX elapsed-time accounting; it does not establish that UART is the only remote latency bottleneck
Full FIFO applies deliberate lossless backpressure rather than simulating physical UART overrun
Nominal 115200 8N1 is fixed; arbitrary baud/control behavior remains incomplete
